Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MedTech Innovations Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MedTech Innovations Inc. had a productive Q2, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance:
1. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
2. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter
3. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
4. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
5. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
6. New product launches and contribution to growth

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Elena will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. Michael, over to you.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Let me address our gross margin performance and offer some insights into supply chain dynamics, which were central to our focus this quarter.

We achieved a robust adjusted gross margin of 68.7% in Q2, representing a 140 basis point improvement year-over-year and 50 basis points sequentially from Q1's 68.2%. This is our eighth straight quarter of margin expansion, lifting the trailing four-quarter average to 68.1%, surpassing our long-term target of 67-69%. GAAP margins stood at 67.9%, after accounting for a $12 million inventory write-down charge from our legacy electrophysiology product line, which we plan to fully phase out by year-end.

Key contributors included a favorable product mix, adding roughly 90 basis points. Our neuromodulation and structural heart offerings, spearheaded by the Vantage bioresorbable stent platform now accounting for more than 15% of cardiovascular revenue, experienced double-digit growth at margins over 75%. This shift compensated for declines in lower-margin commodity disposables, such as our legacy laparoscopic trocars, down 8% as we transition to premium robotic-enabled instruments designed for compatibility with platforms like Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci.

Pricing discipline contributed around 60 basis points. Domestically, we rolled out targeted list price hikes of 4-6% in orthopedics and endoscopy, facing little resistance due to compelling clinical data from the ORTHO-360 trial showing better outcomes than Stryker's Mako in knee arthroplasty. Overseas, we managed reimbursement challenges in Japan, where national health insurance pricing for next-gen pacemakers remained unchanged, but volume gains helped balance it.

Manufacturing efficiencies provided another 40 basis points through better yields. Our Greenfield, Indiana Center of Excellence for precision titanium implant machining reached 98% yields on spinal rods, improved from 92% last year, aided by AI-powered predictive maintenance via our Siemens Digital Industries partnership.

Headwinds included raw material inflation in medical-grade polycarbonate resins and rare earth metals for MRI-compatible neurostimulators, deducting 30 basis points. Elevated freight and logistics from Red Sea issues added 20 basis points of pressure, while FX was a slight 10 basis point drag from a firmer dollar against the euro.

By region, U.S. margins reached a record 71.2%, supported by domestic scale and the 45X tax credit under the Inflation Reduction Act for insulin pump output. EMEA held at 65.8%, holding firm amid MDR delays affecting 10% of our catheter lines, akin to Boston Scientific's Watchman challenges. APAC dipped to 64.5% from China volume-based procurement, but our shift to premium TAVR valves is steadying it.

For full-year 2024, we guide adjusted gross margins to 68.5-69.0%, suggesting further 100 basis point growth, assuming steady FX and resin costs; polysulfone spikes could trim the low end by 20-30 basis points.

On supply chain, our resilience sets us apart in an industry reliant on sterile manufacturing and just-in-time OR deliveries. Post-2022 chip shortages that halted 20% of CRM production, we've dual-sourced 95% of Tier 1 components, up from 70%. For semiconductors in closed-loop glucose monitors and neuromod devices, three foundry partners—including TSMC mature nodes and a U.S. fab through CHIPS Act ties with GlobalFoundries—limited Taiwan earthquake impacts to a 2% wafer dip versus industry 15% shortfalls.

Raw materials see 40% polymer nearshoring to North America, with a long-term deal at Sabic's U.S. site for PEEK in spinal fusion cages, shielding from 18% YTD Asian volatility due to China's controls. Metal powders for custom cranial implants are 60% from Mexico's Querétaro site, halving lead times and avoiding tariffs.

Inventories are at 7.8 months, up from pre-COVID 5.5, to guard against H5N1 glove risks or Ukraine nickel surges for stents. Our Precision Microdrives acquisition internalizes 30% of endoscopy robotics micromotors, aiming for 50% by 2026.

Digitally, SAP S/4HANA covers 80% of sites, integrating IoT for 48-hour disruption visibility—key during Baltimore bridge issues, rerouting 90% of East Coast shipments. Blockchain pilots with IBM for bioresorbable scaffolds ensure EU IVDR compliance by 2025.

Overall, our margin gains show execution amid macro challenges, backed by a stronger supply chain for leadership in electrophysiology and robotics. Back to you, Alex.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Michael, for that thorough update. Now, let's discuss our strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter. Michael, your thoughts?

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, all. Closing out a strong Q2 with 18% year-over-year revenue growth to $1.2 billion—powered by 22% structural heart expansion and steady orthopedics amid supply hurdles—here's our roadmap for Q3. These efforts target leadership in the $500 billion global med devices market, leveraging aging populations, minimally invasive procedure uptake, while tackling inflation and reimbursement shifts.

Our guiding pillars: innovation acceleration, geographic expansion with smart pricing, and operational resilience. Details follow.

First, ramp innovation for 25%+ organic growth in premium segments. Q3 R&D at 12.5% of revenues, about $150 million, advances key items. Central is the EnduraFlow AI-Enabled TAVR Valve global rollout, extending our predicate's 15% U.S. share against Edwards' Sapien. AI optimizes hemodynamics, cutting paravalvular leaks 30% in ORBIT-3 trial; FDA nod expected mid-quarter, projecting $200 million annual revenue by FY2026 at 75% margins.

Robotics sees FlexiArm NeuroNavigation System ramp, da Vinci-like for cranial work. Q3 targets CE Mark filing, Asia first cases, eyeing $1.5 billion market at 28% CAGR. Bioresorbable stents for coronaries—with 30% magnesium degradation vs. Abbott's Absorb—hit Phase II readout end-quarter, tackling 12% restenosis.

Second, expand geographically, targeting 20% revenue lift from APAC/emerging. U.S. (55% mix) grows 15-18% via surgeon training, Kaiser ties, 42% Medicare Advantage reach post-EnduraFlow pass-through.

Europe (25%) aims 12% growth despite MDR (92% compliant on 45 Class III devices), using bundles against pricing pressure; UK post-Brexit wins key.

APAC (18%) eyes 30% surge: China nods for three products like neuromod leads (25% DBS growth per IQVIA); $25 million for India/SEA distributor/KOL build, tapping $10 billion diabetes market with 14-day CGM at 92% MARD.

Third, boost operations amid 8-10% input inflation. Q3 gross margins to 70% via MedTech Shield: dual-source 85% nitinol from U.S./Vietnam, dodging Red Sea; IoT analytics cut plant downtime 15%, turns to 4.2x. Sustainability: 25% Scope 3 cut with recycled ortho polymers for EU CSRD.

Fourth, smart capital use. $1.8 billion cash, 1.8x leverage funds $500M-$2B electrophysiology/digital tuck-ins (one Q3 close); $300 million buybacks at 22x P/E, dividend up 10% to $0.45/share.

This sets Q3 revenues at $1.35-1.40 billion (15-18% YoY), EPS $1.85-1.95, 300 bps margin gain. We're primed for robotics/AI's $100 billion value by 2030 per McKinsey. Over to you, Alex.

Alex Rivera:
Appreciate it, Michael. Moving to the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives. Michael, your perspective?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Alex. Good afternoon. Our pricing and cost efforts were crucial in countering payer pressures, reimbursement flux, and supply inflation from geopolitics on titanium/polymers. We expanded gross margins 210 basis points YoY to 68.2%, boosting adjusted EPS to $1.42, up 15%.

Pricing first: value-based focus shifts from fee-for-service. U.S. (55% revenue) renewed Vizient/Premier deals, gaining 2.5% on cardiology like bioresorbable DES (Abbott Xience-like), tied to 12% lower readmissions from 50,000-patient data.

ASPs rose 1.8% sequentially, offsetting CMS 4.7% OPPS cut on EP devices via mix: structural heart (MitraClip-like TMVR) up 28% YoY, 22% U.S. cardio mix vs. 18%. Offset ortho basket pressure (3-5%) from IDNs like Kaiser.

EMEA (25%): tiered pricing—3.2% premium on AI robotics vs. Intuitive, standard capital. APAC: 4% gains in India/China volumes, Japan 1% dip from NHI.

Pricing added 150 bps to margins, 2.1% core ASP growth net FX erosion.

Costs: $250 million run-rate savings by FY2025, COGS to 31.8% (-190 bps).

Supply opt (40%): 18-month nitinol/PEEK hedges cut inflation to 2.1% from 7%; 20% Mexico/Vietnam shift saves 15% logistics, blockchain for FDA compliance.

Manufacturing (30%): Six Sigma yields up 5.2% in neuromod like Parkinson's DBS; $120 million cobots boost Galway throughput 22%, labor -8%; scrap to 2.9%.

Indirect (30%): ZBB trims SG&A travel/consult 6%, R&D steady 11.5%; AI maintenance cuts service 12%.

Saved $85 million quarterly, covering 3% inflation. Impact: 3.5% op margin to 28.4%, $0.18 EPS add.

Forward: Medicare Advantage shift (50% by 2025), outcomes contracts with Optum on CGM sharing A1c savings; China JVs for disposables. Guide 2% ASP, $100 million FY24 savings, 8-10% growth, 29% margins.

Back to you, Alex.

Alex Rivera:
Great insights, Michael. Next up, procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary. Michael?

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Good afternoon. Procedure volumes lead our growth in structural heart, orthopedics, endoscopy, neuromod. Q2 global tracked volumes rose 18% YoY, sixth double-digit quarter, 105% pre-COVID recovery per our 2.5 million procedure database from 1,200 hospitals—beating IQVIA/Definitive's 14%.

By franchise:

Structural heart: TAVR/TMVR +28%, TAVR 142,000 units +32%, EvoFlex at 22% U.S. share (+4 pts), HeartFlow AI cuts times 22 minutes.

Orthopedics: hips/knees +12% to 95% 2019; cementless hips +16% on Triad implants; revisions +8% on staffing/cement.

Endoscopy: +14%, GI +19% post-USPSTF; VisioScope-X +35% ASC adoption.

Neuromod: SCS +11% to 92% pre-COVID; BurstDR +5 share pts.

Regions:

U.S. (65%): +22% to 112%; ASC ortho 28% vs. 19%; CMS TAVR claims +25%.

Europe (20%): +9% to 98%; EvoFlex +15% UK/Benelux despite German/French cuts.

APAC (10%): +32% >115%; China TAVR +45% 12% share; Japan ortho +25%.

ROW (5%): LatAm +16%, MEA +10%.

Tailwinds: 1.2 million U.S. ortho backlog, 65+ growth 3%, ASP inflation 2.1%.

Headwinds: RN shortages 10-15%, resins/nitinol—dual-sourced Limerick/Singapore.

Initiatives: ProcureAI 92% demand accuracy, 8.2x turns; robotics embeds +15% da Vinci; TAVR bundles 18% margins; China JV $150M.

Guide Q3 +16-19%, U.S. heart high-end; FY 17-20%, $4.8-5.0B revenue +15% organic.

Over to you, Alex.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Michael. Shifting to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. Elena, please share your update.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We're advancing our long-term strategy with strong R&D commitment. Q2 spend hit $152 million, 12.5% of revenue—up 18% YoY, seventh double-digit quarter. FY2024 guide $620-650 million, +15-17% from 2022, targeting value-based care, minimally invasive, digital.

Allocation: cardio 35% ($53M) for $10B structural heart (12% CAGR); ortho/robotics 28%; neuromod/neuro 22%; digital/AI 15%. Shifted 8% to disruptors like AI diagnostics, bioresorbables.

Pipeline: 28 programs (vs. 24 YoY)—7 late-stage, 12 mid, 9 preclin. 5 milestones Q2.

Cardio: AuraResorb™ BVS IDE enrollment done (850 pts), 95% success, 1.2% TLF; FDA H1 2024, $2.5B market.

Robotics/ortho: VertexFlex™ knee robot primary endpoint met—35% less tissue damage, 22% faster recovery vs. conventional; CE Mark, U.S. IDE Q1 2024 w/Mayo; 3x ROI on $180M OrthoRobotics buy.

Neuromod: NeuroPulse™ HF-DBS PULSE-HF interim: 28% NYHA improve, 18% LVEF; Breakthrough Device year-end, EU sales H2 2024.

Regions: U.S. 55% (12 IDEs); Europe 30% (3 CE, €45M early rev); APAC 15% +25% YoY (China NMPA enables).

Returns: 22% R&D-to-revenue, 4 launches +$210M sales +40%. Ahead of 10% industry avg. 6-8 approvals 2024-25, 12-15% growth, 150 bps margins via 65%+ ASP robotics/AI. Risks clinical/reimbursement, offset by data/HTA.

Our engine blends M&A, organic, collabs for $50B robotics, demographics. Back to Alex.

Alex Rivera:
Excellent progress, Elena. Finally, new product launches and their contribution to growth.

New launches since Q1 2023 drove $178 million Q2 revenue—22% of $810 million device sales, +45% YoY, 60% of growth. 72% margins (+300 bps), ASP $12,500, Costa Rica scale.

Flagship: NeoFlex BVS, FDA PMA/CE, magnesium-sirolimus cuts restenosis 28% vs. Xience (ORBITAL-2). U.S. cases +55% to 4,200, 12% share, $92M sales, $8,200 ASP; Japan ramp.

PrecisionNav R1 ortho robot, 510(k), AI haptics/CT, sub-mm alignment, 35% less damage (KEYNOTE). $56M (+20% target), 85 U.S. bases, 22 cases/system/mo; Europe 25%, APAC 30% goal.

VitalSense CGM Pro, de novo, 14-day/8.2% MARD, alerts; $30M, 150k units, UnitedHealthcare path, $450/box.

Regions: U.S. 65% (ASC +10%); EMEA +38%; APAC +60% China NMPA $25B market 16% CAGR.

$450M R&D (6.5%) for >$1B potentials: AI planning, biomaterials, HL7 FHIR. Pipeline: NeoFlex TAVR H1 2025, PrecisionNav spine, VitalSense HTN. New contrib 25-30% FY25 growth, 16-19% organic, 68-70% margins.

Transformative for 200 bps share gain. Back to financials, Michael.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Building on those highlights, we posted solid Q2 financials: $1.2 billion revenue, +18% reported, 19% organic; EPS $1.42 adjusted, +15%. Expenses controlled: OpEx 39.5% revenue, R&D 12.5%, SG&A leverage from scale. Profitability strong at 28.4% op margin. Cash $1.8B, free cash flow $220M. Guidance: FY24 revenue $4.8-5.0B +15% organic, EPS $6.20-6.40, gross margins 68.5-69.0%. Q3 as noted.

Now, I'll hand to Elena for pipeline.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. We're advancing meaningfully in R&D. Thrilled with clinical trials for EnduraFlow TAVR, showing strong efficacy in reducing leaks and improving outcomes.

Pipeline highlights align with earlier: AuraResorb, VertexFlex, NeuroPulse on track, plus robotics integrations and digital tools. Multiple catalysts ahead.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Elena. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions: press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On gross margins and supply chain—any forward risks from resin inflation or Red Sea, and how does dual-sourcing hold up?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, John. We've fortified with 95% dual-sourcing and nearshoring 40% polymers, so recent disruptions like Red Sea or earthquakes had minimal 2% impact vs. peers' 15%. Resins hedged; if polysulfone rises, low-end guide absorbs 20-30 bps. Confident in 68.5-69% FY.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis:
Hi team. On pricing and costs—how sustainable are the 2% ASP gains with payer pushback, and savings run-rate details?

Michael Chen:
Hi Emily. Sustainability high via value evidence: 12% readmission cuts secured GPO uplifts. Mix to premium heart/robotics offsets CMS cuts. Savings $250M run-rate: 40% supply hedges/nearshore, 30% yields/automation, 30% ZBB. $100M FY24 on track.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee:
Thanks. Procedure volumes strong, but Europe lagging—thoughts on recovery there amid reimbursement?

Lisa Patel:
Robert, thanks. Europe at +9% but UK/Benelux +15% on EvoFlex CE. German/French tariffs easing with DRG tweaks; bundles and MDR compliance (92%) position us for H2 acceleration to 12% regional growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Karen Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Karen Wong:
Congrats. On R&D pipeline and new launches—timelines for AuraResorb FDA, and new product ramp risks?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Karen. AuraResorb IDE complete, strong 1.2% TLF; H1 2024 FDA sub on track. Launches like NeoFlex/PrecisionNav exceeding: 12% share quick, 20% over target. Risks managed via trials/partners; 6-8 approvals drive 12-15% growth.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are well-positioned to continue our growth trajectory and deliver long-term value.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
